linkedin_post_draft:
Physical AI cannot exist without microsecond determinism at the edge.

With Boston Dynamics and NVIDIA deepening their collaboration for humanoid robots, the conversation is heavily centered on AI accelerators. But in real-world robotics engineering, inference speed is only half the battle.

Even a sub-10ms neural net inference is useless if your actuator control loop experiences jitter or drops packets.

While developing AuraReflex, I split the architecture:
1. Edge Vision: Streamed OpenCV/YOLO processing for state classification.
2. Deterministic Execution: Non-blocking ESP32 C++ ISRs handling millisecond-accurate reflex responses without RTOS task drift.

High-compute foundation models provide the perception, but deterministic embedded firmware guarantees safety and physical precision.

Robotics engineers: How do you decouple high-jitter inference from your hard real-time motor control loops?
